name: Gamma Persei
description: A naked-eye star 74.6 parsecs away, 31.2 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: radius 31.21 +1.24/-1.15 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 3.894 +/- 0.018 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: mass 3.64 +/- 0.25 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: effective temperature 4589 +/- 58 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 18925: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 13.41 +/- 0.51 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 75 parsecs away whose disc the NPOI measured: 31.2 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 3.894 milliarcseconds, which gives 31.21 solar radii and 4,589 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 18925: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 447071293401293056 (quality A), from 2004A&A...424..727P; Gaia DR3 measures none
